increments.title: A correction round of pure coverage gaps runs test-author and reviewer only
increments.goal: Let the reviewer classify each finding it returns as a coverage gap or a defect, and have the workflow run a round whose findings are all coverage gaps through test-author and reviewer alone, visibly and on the record.
criteria: The reviewer's structured return carries a per-finding classification field that says whether the finding is a coverage gap or a defect; it is a value the reviewer sets, not a phrase the workflow greps out of prose.
When every finding of a round is classified a coverage gap, that correction round runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and does not run the researcher or the implementer.
A round with at least one finding classified a defect runs the full four-agent chain exactly as it does today.
The workflow log()s that it is correcting coverage only when it takes the shortened path.
The reviewer's classification of each finding is recorded in backlog.json alongside the round it belongs to.
The reviewer's own brief states what makes a finding a coverage gap rather than a defect, so the classification is decided the same way twice.
The test suite passes.

return.summary: Give every reviewer finding a required `kind` of coverage-gap or defect, route a round whose findings are all coverage gaps through the test-author and the reviewer alone with a log line saying it is correcting coverage only, and state the standard on the reviewer's page.
return.plan:
GOAL A correction round whose every finding is "the behaviour is right but nothing goes red when it breaks" must run the test-author and the reviewer only. Today the reviewer's finding already carries `fix` (`direct` | `needs-plan`), which decides how much *planning* a correction needs; that field cannot answer *what sort of wrong* the finding is, so a second, orthogonal field is added. Both `workflows/loop.js` and `workflows/agile-loop.js` change, identically. The two scripts deliberately duplicate each other (a workflow script cannot import a sibling) and `agile-loop.js`'s own header says anything changed in one chain belongs in the other; `test-repo.sh`'s driver runs the same modes against both. A change in one file only is a divergence the suite will catch. 1. THE FIELD — VERDICT schema, both workflows In the `VERDICT` constant (`loop.js` ~line 265, `agile-loop.js` ~line 291), `findings.items` gains one property, placed BEFORE `fix`, and added to that item's `required` array (the item keeps `additionalProperties: false`): kind: { type: 'string', enum: ['coverage-gap', 'defect'], description: 'coverage-gap: the behaviour a criterion asks for is present and right, and the ' + 'only thing wrong is that nothing goes red when it breaks — a criterion with no ' + 'test, a case that cannot fail, an assertion that reads something the code always ' + 'produces. Correcting it touches test files alone. defect: everything else, and ' + 'everything you hesitate over — the behaviour, the prose or the diff is wrong. A ' + 'round in which every finding is a coverage-gap is worked by the test-author ' + 'alone: no researcher, no implementer.', }, Required order in `required`: ['claim', 'reproduction', 'criterion', 'kind', 'fix']. Rejected: extending the existing `fix` enum to a third value `coverage`. One field cannot hold two independent answers, and the criterion asks for a field that says whether the finding is a coverage gap or a defect — a value hidden among two defect values does not say that. Rejected too: making `kind` optional. Every routing field in these scripts is opted into, never fallen into. 2. THE ROUTING — both workflows Beside `isDirectFixRound`, add, with a comment in the register of the file (why this exists, what it costs, what it does not skip): function isCoverageOnlyRound(verdict) { const findings = (verdict && Array.isArray(verdict.findings) && verdict.findings) || [] return findings.length > 0 && findings.every((f) => f && f.kind === 'coverage-gap') } A finding with no `kind` at all is therefore a defect for routing purposes — the shortened path is opted into. `isDirectFixRound` gains one guard: a finding counts as direct only when `f.fix === 'direct' && f.kind !== 'coverage-gap'`. A coverage gap has no code to fix, so an implementer-only round could not correct it even if the reviewer marked it `direct`. Every round whose findings are all defects behaves exactly as it does today. In the round loop (`loop.js` ~line 624, `agile-loop.js` ~line 730), replace the single `directFix` line with: const coverageOnly = round > 0 && isCoverageOnlyRound(verdict) const directFix = round > 0 && !coverageOnly && isDirectFixRound(verdict) Both are decided before anything is dispatched and only from the verdict of the round before, so `plan` is always the one an earlier round produced. The round body becomes three branches instead of two: if (coverageOnly) { log() const testsLabel = `tests:${task.id}.${round}` tests = await step(testsLabel, 'Tests', () => agent(, { agentType: 'uroboros:test-author', phase: 'Tests', label: testsLabel, schema: TESTS, })) if (asksTheHuman(testsLabel, tests)) break } else if (directFix) { } else { } and the implementer dispatch that follows is wrapped in `if (!coverageOnly) { ... }`, its `asksTheHuman(buildLabel, build)` break included. The review dispatch, the findings count, the accept/`MAX_CORRECTIONS` logging and everything after are untouched: a coverage-only round is reviewed like any other, which is what keeps it cheap rather than unsafe. Labels are unchanged (`tests:.`, `review:.`), so resume from `backlog.json` keeps working with no change. 3. THE LOG LINE Exactly one `log()` fires on the shortened path, and it must contain the literal phrase `correcting coverage only` — a test asserts on that phrase. `agile-loop.js`: `Increment ${n} round ${round}: every finding is a coverage gap — correcting coverage only, research and implementation skipped, checks carried over from round ${round - 1}.` `loop.js` (no increment ordinal, matching its sibling direct-fix line): `Round ${round}: every finding is a coverage gap — correcting coverage only, research and implementation skipped, checks carried over from round ${round - 1}.` No other path may emit that phrase. 4. THE COVERAGE-ROUND TEST-AUTHOR PROMPT Add `coverageBlock(verdict, round)` beside `directFixBlock`, built the same way (findings numbered, claim / Reproduction / Criterion per line). `agile-loop.js` says "for this increment" where `loop.js` does not, exactly as the two `directFixBlock`s already differ. It must state, in the imperative: - this is correction loop N of MAX_CORRECTIONS and it is a coverage-only round: every finding says the behaviour is already right and only the guard is missing, so nobody planned this round and nobody implements it; - the findings are the whole work order — each reproduction is the spec of one case; - write those cases and nothing else, in the file and style the existing tests for that behaviour use; - the behaviour is already there, so the case passes against the code as it stands and would fail if that behaviour were removed; confirm both and say so in `got` for each case — this round has no implementer to turn a red test green, and a red test reaching the reviewer ends the increment blocked; - test files only, no production code; - a finding you cannot turn into a case goes in `openQuestions`, not into a guess. The test-author's prompt in this round is assembled as: scope block (`agile-loop.js` only, as today) + `coverageBlock(verdict, round)` + `checkList(plan.checks)` + `recordStep(task.id, testsLabel)` + `noDispatch`. `checkList` is included because no implementer runs this round: the commands the round before closed are what the test-author runs to confirm its new case is green, and they are the same ones the reviewer will run. Rejected: amending `agents/test-author.md` for this round. The page says tests must fail first; that rule is right for every other round, and the one round where it inverts is fully described by the prompt the workflow builds. No criterion of this increment asks for the page to change. 5. THE REVIEWER'S BRIEF — agents/reviewer.md In "What you return", the `findings` bullet (lines 111-128), insert `kind` ahead of `fix` and define the standard once, in that bullet and nowhere else on the page: - `coverage-gap` — the behaviour a criterion asks for is present and right in the diff, and the only thing wrong is that nothing goes red when it breaks: a criterion no test would catch, a case that cannot fail, an assertion that reads something the code always produces. The correction touches test files alone. - `defect` — everything else: the behaviour, the prose, or the diff itself is wrong, and correcting it changes something other than a test file. - The tie-break, stated plainly: if you cannot say the correction touches test files alone, it is a `defect`. A round whose findings are all `coverage-gap` is worked by the test-author alone — no researcher, no implementer — so a defect marked `coverage-gap` buys a round that cannot fix it. - `fix` is read only for a `defect`; set `needs-plan` on a coverage gap. Keep the existing `fix` sentences as they are. Do not restate the standard in check 3 ("The tests against the intent") — one home per rule; two wordings drift. The page must contain the literal strings `coverage-gap`, `defect` and the phrase `goes red` (a test greps for all three). 6. README.md The README documents how a round is routed, so it would otherwise describe a rule the scripts no longer follow in full. Two minimal edits, no new section: - in the `LOOP` mermaid subgraph (~line 45, beside the existing `REV -.->|"every finding a direct fix:
no plan, no test"| IMPL`), add `REV -.->|"every finding a coverage gap:
no plan, no fix"| TEST`; - in the paragraph beginning "A finding says how much of the chain its correction needs" (~lines 62-71), add two or three sentences: a finding also says what sort of wrong it is, a coverage gap being one where the behaviour is right and only the guard is missing, and a round of nothing but coverage gaps is worked by the test-author and the reviewer — no plan, no fix, because there is nothing to fix. Nothing else in README.md changes. 7. WHAT IS ALREADY DONE The criterion "the classification is recorded in backlog.json alongside the round" needs no new code: `skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs`'s `record` stores the step return verbatim under the label `review:.`, which carries the round. The new `kind` field is what makes there be something to record; a case in the recorder suite pins that the two meet. OUT OF SCOPE for this increment: the argus-ui test harness, `bin/parse-agent-log`, the collector fixture, `test.sh`'s signing check, the loop skill pages, and `backlog.mjs record` reading stdin. Later increments own each.

return.environment:
Everything runs from the repository root, /home/user/uroboros. Prerequisites: `bash` and `node` (the suites use `node --test` and `node:test`, so Node 18 or newer). No install step and no network: every suite in the repository is zero-dependency, and the npm ones run through their own package's `test` script with no `npm install` first.

Commands the test plan asks anyone to run:
- `bash test-repo.sh` — the repository's own suite, which contains the workflow driver modes and every grep case.
- `node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs` — the backlog recorder suite alone.
- `./test.sh` — every suite in the repository, one after another; it already runs both of the above.

There is no linter and no formatter in this repository. There is no watch mode and no single-case filter for `test-repo.sh`: it is a bash script that prints one `ok`/`FAIL` line per case and exits non-zero when any failed, so a single driver mode is run directly with the driver the script writes, or by reading the `ok`/`FAIL` lines of the whole run.
return.testPlan:
TESTS ARE NEEDED.

I ran nothing: no command was needed to settle a question this plan depends on, so the first run of the list below is the implementer's. Nothing in the suite is known to be red; `test-repo.sh` and the recorder suite are expected green on the current checkout, and the new cases below are expected red until the implementation lands — except case D, which is green from the start and says so.

THE TWO TEST FILES AND THEIR CONVENTIONS

(1) /home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh — bash, no framework. Two helpers at the top define a case: `ok "<sentence>"` and `no "<sentence>"`, each printing one line; the script exits non-zero when any case failed. Sections are separated by `echo` + `echo "=== <section title>"`. Every case carries a comment above it saying which finding or run it came from and what broke without it. Inside it, a heredoc (`cat >"$driver_tmp/driver.js" <<'JS' ... JS`) writes a Node driver that loads a workflow script with `new AsyncFunction`, stubs `agent`, `log` and `phase`, and asserts on the labels dispatched, the prompts sent and the lines logged. The driver's shape: string markers in `DISJOINT_MARKERS` (a startup guard asserts no marker is a substring of another), fixture return objects, `contextFor(mode)` giving the per-mode stubs, `returnFor(label)` mapping a dispatch label to its fixture, then one `else if (mode === 'wN')` branch of assertions in `main()`. `assertEqualArrays(labels, expected, msg)` pins the exact dispatch sequence; `assertTrue(cond, msg)` everything else. A mode is wired up by a `run_driver "$wf" wN "$wf_name: <sentence>"` line inside the `for wf in loop.js agile-loop.js` loop near the end. `isAgile` is true for agile-loop.js; the closing label is `replan:i1` there and `close:i1` in the plain loop.
Run it with: `bash test-repo.sh`

(2) /home/user/uroboros/skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs — `node:test` with `node:assert/strict`. Each case is a top-level `test('<sentence describing the rule>', () => { ... })`. Helpers already in the file: `tmpDir()`, `writeJson(dir, name, value)`, `run(args)` (executes the CLI, returns stdout), `runFails(args)`, `backlogTemplate(increments)`, `incrementPayload(id, title)`. The pattern of every record case: make a temp dir, `run(['init', backlogPath, writeJson(...)])`, `run(['record', ...])`, then `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(backlogPath, 'utf8'))` and assert on the structure.
Run it with: `node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs`

CASE A — a round whose every finding is a coverage gap runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and says so.
Proves: criteria 2 and 4 (coverage-only round skips researcher and implementer; the workflow log()s that it is correcting coverage only), and criterion 1 in use.
Level: integration, through the workflow driver. File: test-repo.sh. New driver mode `w17`, run against BOTH workflows inside the existing `for wf` loop.
Setup: add markers `MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM` and `MARKER-COVERAGE-REPRODUCTION` to `DISJOINT_MARKERS`. Add a fixture beside `verdictReturnWithDirectFinding`:
  const verdictReturnWithCoverageFinding = { findings: [{ claim: 'MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM', reproduction: 'MARKER-COVERAGE-REPRODUCTION', criterion: 'none', kind: 'coverage-gap', fix: 'needs-plan' }], reason: 'MARKER-VERDICT-REASON', questions: [], summary: 'verdict summary' }
Add to `contextFor`: case 'w17' returns `{ stateReturn: { exists: false, backlogJson: '', summary: '' }, decomposeReturn: decomposeReturnOne, researchReturn: planReturn, verdictFor: (label) => (label === 'review:i1.0' ? verdictReturnWithCoverageFinding : verdictReturnClean) }`.
Input/state: a fresh run, round 0 clean, round 0's review returning that one coverage-gap finding.
Expected:
  - `assertEqualArrays(labels, ['load-state', 'decompose', 'research:i1.0', 'tests:i1.0', 'implement:i1.0', 'review:i1.0', 'tests:i1.1', 'review:i1.1', closeLabel, 'publish'], ...)` — no `research:i1.1` and no `implement:i1.1`.
  - the `tests:i1.1` prompt contains `MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM` and `MARKER-COVERAGE-REPRODUCTION`.
  - the `tests:i1.1` prompt contains `CHECK-MARKER` (the checks the round before closed).
  - the `tests:i1.1` prompt does NOT contain `TESTPLAN_MARKER` — no researcher wrote one this round, so a stale plan must not be replayed into it.
  - the `review:i1.1` prompt contains `CHECK-MARKER` and does NOT contain `MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM` (the reviewer stays independent of the finding it wrote).
  - `logs.some((l) => l.includes('correcting coverage only'))` is true.
  - `result.blockedOnHuman` is an empty array (the round runs to a clean close).
run_driver line: `run_driver "$wf" w17 "$wf_name: a correction round whose findings are all coverage gaps runs the test-author and the reviewer alone, and logs that it is correcting coverage only"`
Command that runs just it: `bash test-repo.sh` (its `ok`/`FAIL` line is the case).

CASE B — a round with one coverage gap and one defect runs the full four-agent chain.
Proves: criterion 3 (at least one defect ⇒ the chain today).
Level and file: as case A. New driver mode `w18`, both workflows.
Setup: a fixture whose `findings` array holds the coverage-gap finding of case A AND a defect finding `{ claim: 'MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM', reproduction: 'MARKER-FINDING-REPRODUCTION', criterion: 'MARKER-FINDING-CRITERION', kind: 'defect', fix: 'needs-plan' }`. `contextFor` case 'w18' mirrors w17 with that fixture.
Expected:
  - `assertEqualArrays(labels, ['load-state', 'decompose', 'research:i1.0', 'tests:i1.0', 'implement:i1.0', 'review:i1.0', 'research:i1.1', 'tests:i1.1', 'implement:i1.1', 'review:i1.1', closeLabel, 'publish'], ...)`.
  - no line of `logs` contains `correcting coverage only`.
  - the `research:i1.1` prompt contains BOTH `MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM` and `MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM` — a mixed round drops neither finding.
run_driver line: `run_driver "$wf" w18 "$wf_name: a correction round with one defect among its coverage gaps runs the full chain"`

CASE C — a coverage gap the reviewer also marked a direct fix is not handed to the implementer alone.
Proves: the guard in `isDirectFixRound`; the repeat/conflict edge of criterion 2 against the existing fast path.
Level and file: as case A. New driver mode `w19`, both workflows.
Setup: a fixture identical to case A's but with `fix: 'direct'` on the coverage-gap finding. `contextFor` case 'w19' mirrors w17 with it.
Expected: the same label array as case A (`tests:i1.1` and `review:i1.1`, no `implement:i1.1`), and `logs.some((l) => l.includes('correcting coverage only'))` true.
run_driver line: `run_driver "$wf" w19 "$wf_name: a coverage gap marked a direct fix still goes to the test-author, not to the implementer alone"`

CASE D — a recorded verdict keeps each finding's classification, under the label that carries the round.
Proves: criterion 5. Expected GREEN from the first run: `record` already stores the step return verbatim, and this case is what pins that the new field survives into the run state. Say exactly that in the case's `got` — do not hunt a failure for it.
Level: unit, against the CLI. File: /home/user/uroboros/skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs. New `test(...)` at the end of the record group (after the case at line 193).
Name: `test('record keeps each finding's classification in the verdict it stores under the round's label', ...)`.
Input/state: `tmpDir()`; `run(['init', backlogPath, writeJson(dir, 'init.json', backlogTemplate([incrementPayload('i1', 'First')]))])`; a payload `{ findings: [{ claim: 'no guard', reproduction: 'delete the container, nothing goes red', criterion: 'c1', kind: 'coverage-gap', fix: 'needs-plan' }, { claim: 'wrong number', reproduction: 'x at line 3', criterion: 'c2', kind: 'defect', fix: 'direct' }], reason: 'another round', questions: [], summary: 'verdict summary' }` recorded with `run(['record', backlogPath, 'i1', 'review:i1.1', writeJson(dir, 'payload.json', payload)])`.
Expected: reading the file back, the increment `i1` has exactly one step, its `label` is `review:i1.1` (the round is in the label), and `step.return.findings.map((f) => f.kind)` deep-equals `['coverage-gap', 'defect']`.
Command that runs just it: `node --test skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.test.mjs`

FIXTURE MAINTENANCE (not new cases — edits the existing ones need so they keep proving what they were written for)
- `verdictReturnWithDirectFinding` (test-repo.sh ~line 381) gains `kind: 'defect'`, so w16 keeps proving the direct-fix path under the new field.
- `verdictReturnWithFinding` (~line 365) deliberately keeps NO `kind` key at all: it is the missing-field guard, and w10's existing exact-label assertion already proves such a round runs the full chain. Add one assertion to w10: no line of `logs` contains `correcting coverage only`.

CASE E — the reviewer's page states what makes a finding a coverage gap.
Proves: criterion 6.
Level: static, a grep case. File: test-repo.sh, in the block that already greps `$reviewer_page` (~lines 176-186), added directly after it with a comment saying why.
Expected: one `ok`/`no` case that passes only when `agents/reviewer.md` contains all three of the literals `coverage-gap`, `defect` and `goes red`; the `no` branch names which of the three is missing.
Command that runs just it: `bash test-repo.sh`

CASE F — each workflow's verdict schema offers the classification its routing reads.
Proves: criterion 1 (it is a value the reviewer sets, not a phrase greped out of prose). Without it, a script could route on `f.kind` while no reviewer could ever set it, and every driver mode above would still pass — the driver stubs never validate a schema.
Level: static, a grep case per workflow. File: test-repo.sh, in the existing `for f in loop.js agile-loop.js` grep loop area (~lines 161-170) or a new case beside it with its own comment.
Expected: for each of `workflows/loop.js` and `workflows/agile-loop.js`, the file contains both `'coverage-gap'` and `'defect'` as quoted literals; failing names the file.
Command that runs just it: `bash test-repo.sh`

LEFT UNTESTED, AND WHY
- The README edits: no criterion of this increment asks for them, and a grep would pin wording without proving behaviour.
- The exact prose of `coverageBlock` beyond the markers and the checks the driver asserts on: the rest is instruction for an LLM, and pinning its sentences would make every later rewording a red test.
- Whether a reviewer classifies a given finding correctly: that is a judgment no test can make; the brief is what makes it repeatable, and case E proves the brief states it.
- Resume of a coverage-only round from recorded state: the labels are unchanged (`tests:<id>.<round>`), so w2 and w9 already cover the resume mechanism.
- The tools under tools/ : untouched by this increment.

cases.case: A — a round whose every finding is a coverage gap runs the test-author and the reviewer only, and says so.
cases.testName: run_driver w17 (both loop.js and agile-loop.js): "a correction round whose findings are all coverage gaps runs the test-author and the reviewer alone, and logs that it is correcting coverage only"
cases.expected: labels are ['load-state','decompose','research:i1.0','tests:i1.0','implement:i1.0','review:i1.0','tests:i1.1','review:i1.1',closeLabel,'publish'] — no research:i1.1, no implement:i1.1; tests:i1.1 carries MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM, MARKER-COVERAGE-REPRODUCTION and CHECK-MARKER but not TESTPLAN_MARKER; review:i1.1 carries CHECK-MARKER but not MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM; some log line includes 'correcting coverage only'; result.blockedOnHuman is empty.
cases.got: FAIL for both workflows. loop.js: "a correction round whose findings are all coverage gaps did not skip exactly the researcher and the implementer — expected [\"load-state\",\"decompose\",\"research:i1.0\",\"tests:i1.0\",\"implement:i1.0\",\"review:i1.0\",\"tests:i1.1\",\"review:i1.1\",\"close:i1\",\"publish\"] got [\"load-state\",\"decompose\",\"research:i1.0\",\"tests:i1.0\",\"implement:i1.0\",\"review:i1.0\",\"research:i1.1\",\"tests:i1.1\",\"implement:i1.1\",\"review:i1.1\",\"close:i1\",\"publish\"]" plus "the coverage-only round's test-author prompt does not carry MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM", "...MARKER-COVERAGE-REPRODUCTION", "...does not carry the checks the round before closed", "...carries a stale test plan no researcher wrote this round", and "the workflow never logged that it is correcting coverage only". agile-loop.js failed the same five assertions with replan:i1 as the close label. The failures are the missing coverage-only routing itself, not an import error or typo.

cases.case: B — a round with one coverage gap and one defect runs the full four-agent chain.
cases.testName: run_driver w18 (both loop.js and agile-loop.js): "a correction round with one defect among its coverage gaps runs the full chain"
cases.expected: labels are the full chain ['load-state','decompose','research:i1.0','tests:i1.0','implement:i1.0','review:i1.0','research:i1.1','tests:i1.1','implement:i1.1','review:i1.1',closeLabel,'publish']; no log line contains 'correcting coverage only'; research:i1.1 carries both MARKER-FINDING-CLAIM and MARKER-COVERAGE-CLAIM.
cases.got: PASS on both workflows already, before any implementation change: `ok — loop.js: a correction round with one defect among its coverage gaps runs the full chain` and the same for agile-loop.js. This is not a mistake in the case — today's code has no coverage-only shortcut at all, so every correction round already runs the unabridged chain and the researcher already receives every finding's claim regardless of a 'kind' field nobody reads yet. Criterion 3 only asks that this stay true once the shortcut exists, so the case is a real regression guard, not a false pass; but it contradicts the plan's opening claim that every case below (bar D) is red until the implementation lands. Recorded verbatim in openQuestions.

cases.case: C — a coverage gap the reviewer also marked a direct fix is not handed to the implementer alone.
cases.testName: run_driver w19 (both loop.js and agile-loop.js): "a coverage gap marked a direct fix still goes to the test-author, not to the implementer alone"
cases.expected: same label array as case A (tests:i1.1 and review:i1.1, no implement:i1.1), and some log line includes 'correcting coverage only'.
cases.got: FAIL for both workflows. loop.js: "a coverage gap marked a direct fix was routed to the implementer alone instead of the test-author — expected [...,\"tests:i1.1\",\"review:i1.1\",\"close:i1\",\"publish\"] got [...,\"implement:i1.1\",\"review:i1.1\",\"close:i1\",\"publish\"]" plus "the workflow never logged that it is correcting coverage only". agile-loop.js failed the same two assertions with replan:i1. This confirms today's existing direct-fix fast path (built for w16) still swallows a coverage-gap finding that happens to carry fix:'direct', exactly the conflict the case is written to catch.

cases.case: D — a recorded verdict keeps each finding's classification, under the label that carries the round.
cases.testName: record keeps each finding's classification in the verdict it stores under the round's label
cases.expected: reading backlog.json back after `record ... i1 review:i1.1 <payload>`, increment i1 has exactly one step, its label is 'review:i1.1', and step.return.findings.map(f => f.kind) deep-equals ['coverage-gap', 'defect'].
cases.got: PASS from the first run, as the plan says it must be: `ok 8 - record keeps each finding's classification in the verdict it stores under the round's label`. `record` already stores the step return object verbatim with no field-level filtering, so a 'kind' key on each finding survives into the file untouched — this case pins that fact rather than hunting a failure that does not exist.

cases.case: Fixture maintenance — verdictReturnWithDirectFinding gains kind: 'defect' (w16 keeps proving the direct-fix path under the new field).

return.summary:
Opening cut of the seven-finding issue into six increments, ordered risky-first. Criterion-to-increment map, one criterion each: coverage-only-round takes the shortened-correction-round criterion and the visibility criterion (workflow log() plus the reviewer's classification recorded in backlog.json with the round); ui-harness-null takes the installFakes-returns-null criterion and the harness-proves-itself criterion; run-report takes the parse-agent-log workflow-run-directory criterion including the retro skill's instructions; agent-affordances takes the backlog.mjs record stdin criterion and the documented collector start/stop criterion; signing-check takes the ./test.sh signing-verification criterion and the './test.sh is green' criterion; liveness-docs takes the loop-skill liveness criterion.

Why this cut. Findings 1 and 2 of the issue are one delivery, not two: a classification the reviewer sets is worthless until the workflow branches on it, and a branch nobody can see in the log or the backlog is not reviewable, so the field, the branch, the log line and the record land together. It goes first because it is the largest and most load-bearing change and because it rewrites how every later correction round in this run behaves — learning it early is the point. Findings 2 of the issue (the UI harness) goes second: it is the other risky one, since making getElementById return null can turn existing green cases red and the increment has to decide, case by case, whether each was asserting against markup the page never wrote. I put the recorder-stdin fix and the collector fixture into one increment because they are one delivery from the reader's side — an agent stops improvising around missing tooling, and both are named in the same agent brief page — and because two separate chains editing that page would collide for no gain. I rejected splitting the UI harness into 'return null' and 'correct the cases', which is the classic half-increment that leaves the suite red; I rejected splitting parse-agent-log into a tool change and a retro-skill change, since a mode nothing points at is code nobody asked for; and I rejected merging the signing check with the agent-affordances increment, because verifying the environment and giving agents a tool are judged against different evidence.

What the run has to settle that I could not. The shape of the reviewer's structured return and where the workflow decides to run a correction round are facts I do not have, so coverage-only-round is cut to make its researcher establish them first; the increment states the outcome the run needs and names no file or function. Likewise whether ./test.sh can sign a commit at all in this environment is unknown, so signing-check carries an explicit criterion asking the run to choose and justify the behaviour when signing is legitimately unconfigured, rather than putting that to the human and ending the run. The out-of-scope list is honoured: nothing here touches the resume mechanism, the reviewer's standard for rejecting a round, the two open findings of 2026-08-07-agile-loop-optimizations, or the timeline feature.
